title: Walk Down a New Street
description: Walk down a street you have never walked down. It is probably closer than you think. When you get back, write down where you ended up.

rubric.ideal: I turned into a road two streets over from mine that I had never once walked into; it bends left and dead ends behind the back of a supermarket.
There was a porch with about nine wind chimes on it, a repair shop I never knew existed, and a steep bit halfway along that I did not expect.
It was odd being somewhere this close to my own door that I had never actually seen on foot before.

title: Ride to the End of the Line
description: Get on the bus or train that stops nearest you and stay on until it stops going anywhere. Look around for ten minutes, photograph the last stop, then come back.

title: Take Three Wrong Turns
description: Leave your door, and at the first three corners turn the way you never turn. Then find your own way back without asking your phone.

title: Go Into the Shop You Always Pass
description: The one you have walked past a hundred times and never once entered. Go in. You do not have to buy anything; you just have to find out what is in there.

title: Sit on the Bench You Always Walk Past
description: There is a bench on your usual route that you have never once used. Sit on it for five minutes and work out what it is pointed at.

title: Go Inside the Oldest Building You Can Walk To
description: A church, a museum, a town hall; whatever has been standing the longest. Get through the door and stay ten minutes.
